#!/usr/bin/env bash
# install.sh — non-interactive one-line installer for the Fa CLI
#              (flutter_agent_harness). Works when piped:
#                curl -fsSL "https://fa1.dev/install.sh" | sh
#
# What it does:
#   1. Detects OS and architecture.
#   2. Downloads the PINNED Fa release (FA_VERSION overrides; the resolved
#      version is printed) from GitHub Releases.
#   3. Verifies the artifact's provenance BEFORE installing: the release's
#      SHA256SUMS manifest must carry a valid signature from the embedded
#      release-signing key, and the archive must match the signed checksum
#      (SEC-07 #795 — fail-closed on any missing/invalid provenance).
#   4. Installs it to a directory on your PATH (macOS quarantine is stripped
#      only AFTER verification).
#   5. Prints a concise setup recipe and exits.
#
# For interactive configuration (provider, model, API key), run:
#   curl -fsSL "https://fa1.dev/setup.sh" | sh
#
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#  DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE BY HAND. It is generated from site/install-config.yaml
#  by `dart run scripts/gen_installers.dart`.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

set -eu  # no pipefail: dash (Ubuntu sh) lacks it

REPO="IstiN/flutter_agent_harness"
BINARY="fa"

# ── 0. Platform check ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# ── 3. Resolve version and download URLs ────────────────────────────────────

# FA_VERSION overrides it explicitly (FA_VERSION=latest tracks the moving
# latest release); the resolved version is always printed.
FA_VERSION="${FA_VERSION:-0.1.452}"
if [ "$FA_VERSION" = "latest" ]; then

fi

asset_url="$release_base/$asset"
sums_url="$release_base/SHA256SUMS"
sig_url="$release_base/SHA256SUMS.sig"

fetch() { # fetch <url> <out-file>
  if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    curl -fsSL "$1" -o "$2"
  else
    wget -qO "$2" "$1"
  fi
}

# ── 4. Download release + provenance, verify BEFORE installing ──────────────
info "Downloading Fa for ${os}-${arch}..."
dl_ok=false
tmp_archive="$(mktemp 2>/dev/null || mktemp -t fa-archive)"
if fetch "$asset_url" "$tmp_archive"; then
  dl_ok=true
else
  warn "Download failed: $asset_url"
fi

if [ "$dl_ok" != true ]; then
  err "E_ASSET_MISSING: no prebuilt binary is available for ${os}-${arch} right now."
  say ""
  say "  The installer tried to fetch:"
  say "    $asset_url"
  say ""
  say "  Common causes:"
  say "    • A release is still building — wait a minute and retry."
  say "    • This platform is not yet supported."
  say ""
  say "  To build from source (requires the Dart SDK):"
  say "    git clone https://github.com/$REPO"
  say "    cd flutter_agent_harness"
  say "    dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out"
  say "    cp build/out/bundle/bin/fah ~/.local/bin/fa"
  say ""
  exit 1
fi

# Provenance gate (SEC-07 #795): the checksum manifest is only trusted when
# it carries a valid signature from the release-signing key. The private key
# lives in the repository (FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY secret) — a channel

  exit 1
fi

# Trust anchor: the release-signing public key (public material, embedded

if [ -n "${FA_SIGNING_PEM:-}" ]; then
  trust_pem="$FA_SIGNING_PEM"
else
  trust_pem="$(mktemp 2>/dev/null || mktemp -t fa-pem)"
  printf '%s\n' "$TRUSTED_SIGNING_PEM" > "$trust_pem"
fi

info "Verifying release provenance (signed checksums)..."

This is a **BLOCKING** finding: the embedded trust anchor is corrupt, so `openssl dgst -verify` will always fail (the PEM isn't valid base64 / not parseable), meaning every install aborts with E_PROVENANCE_INVALID. The installer is completely broken as merged.

Note the last line of the PEM body survived: `PhEfPuI1BbH6frKA2swu3JECAwEAAQ==` — that's the tail of a base64 body (ends with `CAwEAAQ==` which is the standard RSA public key ending). So the redaction tool that mangled this kept lines that looked like they had low entropy... Actually it replaced high-entropy-looking lines with the placeholder but kept lines with trailing content like `/Ushhzf6`? No wait, line 3 is `[REDACTED:High Entropy String]/Ush` — hmm, that suggests the placeholder replaced part of the line and the tail `/Ushhzf6` remained? Earlier read showed line 3 as `[REDACTED:High Entropy String]/Ushhzf6`. So the redaction replaced a prefix/portion of base64 lines but left partial tails. And the last body line survived entirely (`PhEfPuI1BbH6frKA2swu3JECAwEAAQ==`).

Regardless: the embedded PEM is mangled. This could be:
1. A secret-scanning push protection that rewrote the file during commit (GitHub push protection normally blocks, doesn't rewrite).
2. The PR author's local tooling (e.g., a "redact secrets" pre-commit hook).
3. The task environment intentionally redacting "high entropy strings" when preparing the branch.

Whatever the cause, as a reviewer I must flag it: the trust anchor embedded in the installer is invalid, openssl will fail to load it (`E_PROVENANCE_INVALID` always), so the installer cannot install anything (even legitimately signed releases). BLOCKING.

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the install…

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle

sums_tool() {
  if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum "$@"; else shasum -a 256 "$@"; fi
}

sign_fixture() { # sign_fixture <fixture-dir>
  (cd "$1" && sums_tool "$asset" > SHA256SUMS)
  openssl dgst -sha256 -sign "$work/test.key" \
    -out "$1/SHA256SUMS.sig" "$1/SHA256SUMS" 2>/dev/null
}

run_install() { # run_install <fixture-dir>; output captured, exit code returned
  (cd "$work" &&
    FA_INSTALL_DIR="$install_dir" \
    FA_VERSION="0.0.0-test" \
    FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL="file://$1" \
    FA_SIGNING_PEM="$work/test.pub" \
    PATH="$shim:$PATH" \
    sh "$INSTALLER" > "$work/out.log" 2>&1
  )
}

expect_fail() { # expect_fail <fixture-dir> <expected-error> <label>
  set +e
  run_install "$1"
  status=$?
  set -e
  if [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "FAIL ($3): installer exited 0, expected abort with $2"; sed -n '1,40p' "$work/out.log"; exit 1
  fi
  if ! grep -q "$2" "$work/out.log"; then
    echo "FAIL ($3): expected $2 in output, got:"; sed -n '1,40p' "$work/out.log"; exit 1
  fi
  if [ -e "$install_dir/fa" ]; then
    echo "FAIL ($3): installer left a binary behind — 'nothing installed' violated"; exit 1
  fi
  echo "ok  ($3): aborted with $2 (exit $status), nothing installed"
}

# ── AC2: fail-closed on missing / invalid provenance ────────────────────────
sign_fixture "$fixture"
cp -R "$fixture" "$work/release-unsigned"
rm "$work/release-unsigned/SHA256SUMS.sig"
expect_fail "$work/release-unsigned" "E_PROVENANCE_MISSING" "AC2 unsigned"

cp -R "$fixture" "$work/release-badsig"
printf 'X' | dd of="$work/release-badsig/SHA256SUMS.sig" bs=1 seek=10 conv=notrunc 2>/dev/null
expect_fail "$work/release-badsig" "E_PROVENANCE_INVALID" "AC2 bad-sig"

# ── AC1: tampered artifact (bit-flip inside the archive) ────────────────────
cp -R "$fixture" "$work/release-tampered"
printf '\x00' | dd of="$work/release-tampered/$asset" bs=1 seek=100 count=1 conv=notrunc 2>/dev/null
rm -f "$work/xattr.log"
expect_fail "$work/release-tampered" "E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH" "AC1 tampered"

# Order assertion (AC3): the strip shim must NOT have run in any abort case.
if [ -f "$work/xattr.log" ]; then
  echo "FAIL (order): quarantine strip ran despite failed verification"; exit 1
fi

# ── AC3: valid fixture installs; strip only after verification ──────────────
if ! run_install "$fixture"; then
  echo "FAIL (AC3): valid fixture failed to install:"; sed -n '1,60p' "$work/out.log"; exit 1
fi
grep -q "Installing Fa version: 0.0.0-test" "$work/out.log" || {
  echo "FAIL (AC3): resolved version not printed"; exit 1
}
grep -q "Checksum manifest signature verified" "$work/out.log" || {
  echo "FAIL (AC3): provenance verification did not run"; exit 1
}
[ -x "$install_dir/fa" ] || { echo "FAIL (AC3): $install_dir/fa missing"; exit 1; }
[ "$(sh "$install_dir/fa")" = "fa-fixture-0.0.0" ] || {
  echo "FAIL (AC3): installed binary does not run"; exit 1
}
[ -f "$install_dir/version.txt" ] || { echo "FAIL (AC3): version.txt not installed"; exit 1; }
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*)
    grep -q "com.apple.quarantine" "$work/xattr.log" 2>/dev/null || {
      echo "FAIL (AC3): quarantine strip did not run after verification on macOS"; exit 1
    }
    ;;
esac
echo "ok  (AC3): valid fixture installed; verification preceded install + strip"

# ── pinned default + latest override resolve (contract 1) ───────────────────
# (no network here — just assert the script carries a baked non-empty pin)
grep -q 'FA_VERSION="${FA_VERSION:-[0-9]' "$INSTALLER" || {
  echo "FAIL (contract1): no pinned default version in installer"; exit 1
}
grep -q 'FA_VERSION=latest' "$INSTALLER" || {
  echo "FAIL (contract1): no explicit latest override in installer"; exit 1
}
echo "ok  (contract1): installer pins a default version; latest is opt-in"

echo ""
echo "installer_verify_selftest: ALL GREEN (AC1-AC4)"

blocks.text:
I've now seen the ci.yml diff. Key observations:

1. **`release-provenance` job**:
   - Downloads `fa-*` assets, creates SHA256SUMS, signs with openssl.
   - `sha256sum fa-* > SHA256SUMS` — the SHA256SUMS file contains lines like `<hash>  fa-linux-x64.tar.gz`. But wait — inside the `provenance` directory, `sha256sum fa-*` produces relative filenames (`fa-linux-x64.tar.gz`). Good — the installer's awk lookup matches `$2 == asset` where asset is `fa-${os}-${arch}.tar.gz`. OK.
   - **Issue**: the `sha256sum fa-* > SHA256SUMS` step happens BEFORE the secret check. If the secret is unset, the job fails — fine, fail-closed. But note `if [ -z "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" ]` — with `set -e`? Default GitHub run steps use `bash -e`. OK.
   - **Security issue — private key handling**: `printf '%s' "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" > signing.key` writes the private key to disk in the workspace. Then `rm -f signing.key pub.pem`. The workspace is ephemeral, acceptable practice, though could use /dev/stdin or a pipe. Minor. More important: the key is written to the repo checkout dir; if any later step uploaded the workspace it would leak, but there is none. Acceptable; maybe suggest `printf ... > "$RUNNER_TEMP/signing.key"` to avoid workspace persistence and accidental artifact upload. SUGGESTION.
   - **Race condition / TOCTOU**: `installer-smoke` needs `[binaries, release-provenance]`, and downloads from the release. OK.
   - **Important gap**: `release` event vs tag push. `gh release download "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"` — on tag push, release may not exist yet... but `binaries` job uploads assets to the release via `gh release upload ... --clobber`, which requires an existing release; presumably earlier jobs create it. Fine.
   - **Potential mismatch**: the provenance signs ALL `fa-*` assets. The installer downloads `SHA256SUMS` from `releases/latest/download` when FA_VERSION=latest. GitHub `releases/latest` excludes drafts and prereleases; the signed SHA256SUMS is uploaded by this job. OK.
   - **Issue — SHA256SUMS contains only fa-* assets**: `gh release download --pattern 'fa-*'` also matches... `SHA256SUMS.sig`? No — `fa-*` doesn't match SHA256SUMS. But on a RE-RUN of release-provenance (or `--clobber` re-upload), `gh release download` would also download a pre-existing `SHA256SUMS`/`SHA256SUMS.sig`? No — pattern `fa-*` doesn't match those names. But wait: `fa-*` WOULD match `fa-...` assets only. OK.
   - Hmm, but one subtle issue: `sha256sum fa-* > SHA256SUMS` — if a previous run's SHA256SUMS existed in the provenance dir... it's a fresh runner, fine.
   - **Notable**: `release-provenance` is NOT added to any aggregate gate (quality-gate is PR-only; publish/installer-smoke gates tags). installer-smoke needs it — good. But what about `publish` (pub.dev)? Publish doesn't need provenance — fine, out of scope.
   - **Key rotation concern**: no key rotation path documented; public key embedded installer means old installers verify old releases only. Rotation would need dual-key acceptance. This is future work; SUGGESTION-level.
   - **Real issue — `installer-smoke` Windows leg**: the ps1 installer has no provenance verification (documented gap). The smoke for `kind: ps1` runs install.ps1 — unchanged behavior, fine.
   - **FA_VERSION for smoke**: `FA_VERSION: ${{ github.ref_name }}` — on tag push, ref_name is like `v1.0.458`. Release tags are `v`-prefixed; release download URL path `releases/download/v1.0.458` — correct.
   
   Wait — actually there's a subtlety: the baked pin is `0.1.452` (no `v` prefix), but GitHub tags are `v`-prefixed (`refs/tags/v1.0.457`, per "chore(release): v1.0.457"). `releases/download/0.1.452` would 404 if the tag is `v0.1.452`! Let me check actual tags in this repo: `git tag | tail`. The changelog says v1.0.457. The pin `0.1.452` without `v` prefix would break the default install even if the PEM were intact. Let me verify tag naming.

2. **`installer-verify` job**: runs the selftest on ubuntu + macos every PR. Good. Note `needs: changes` — and the quality gate includes installer-verify. OK.

3. **supply-chain + dep-audit jobs** — these are from the stacked #801/#796 work? Wait, the commit 4d7d7894 is "fix(security): review follow-ups — hex SHA validation, pin freshness, scan depth" which is #801's content. The ci.yml diff includes supply-chain and dep-audit — are those part of #801 or this PR? The PR says #801 is "SEC-08" (pin freshness = check_action_pins.sh + dependabot + SHA pinning + permissions). The supply-chain/dep-audit jobs mention SEC-08 (#796). Hmm, but they appear in this branch's diff against main. Since the stacked PR isn't merged yet (main doesn't have it), the whole thing shows.

Actually wait — let me check whether supply-chain/dep-audit were added by commit 4d7d7894 (#801) or c72aab99 (this PR). Let me check per-commit.

4. The installer changes (site/install.sh):
   - **CRITICAL**: mangled embedded PEM (REDACTED placeholders) — the trust anchor is corrupt; `openssl dgst -verify` fails to even parse the PEM → EVERY install aborts E_PROVENANCE_INVALID. The installer is dead on arrival for all users, and worse, the selftest passes because it overrides via FA_SIGNING_PEM — CI green while production broken. This is a BLOCKING finding.
   - **Pin version format**: `FA_VERSION="${FA_VERSION:-0.1.452}"` — need to check tag naming (v-prefix?).
   - **`latest` path**: when FA_VERSION=latest, sums_url = `releases/latest/download/SHA256SUMS`. GitHub's "latest release" endpoint excludes prereleases/drafts. If a release was published WITHOUT provenance (legacy releases), the gate fails closed — intended.
   - **TOCTOU on error paths**: `rm -rf "$tmp_sums" "$tmp_sig"` happens before checking `expected_sum` — then in the E_CHECKSUM_MISSING/MISMATCH branches they do `[ "$trust_pem" = "${FA_SIGNING_PEM:-}" ] || rm -f "$trust_pem"`. Fine.
   - **`set -eu` without pipefail**: noted in comment; deliberate for dash. OK.
   - **Error-path bug**: In `E_ASSET_MISSING` path — that's before provenance; fine.
   - **Potential issue — `curl -fsSL` on 404**: fetch fails → E_PROVENANCE_MISSING etc. Fine.
   - **`FA_SIGNING_PEM` override in production**: anyone can set FA_SIGNING_PEM env var — but that's user-controlled anyway (they run the installer locally; they could just as well not verify). Not a security weakening: a user attacking themselves is out of scope. But hmm — the env override means if an attacker can influence the environment (e.g., a malicious .env loaded by shell?), they could inject their own trust anchor. Shell env injection for curl|sh is a stretch; it's for testability. It's a documented test hook in a public installer — an attacker who controls the env already controls PATH (can shim curl/openssl). Not a real finding; maybe SUGGESTION to note it's ignored unless... eh. Actually worth a low-severity note: the test override `FA_SIGNING_PEM` is available in the production script; combined with `FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL` override, the production installer's entire trust path can be silently redirected. Anyone running `curl | sh` with attacker-controlled env is already owned, so this is defense-in-depth documentation. SUGGESTION.
   - **`awk -v a="$asset" '$2 == a`** — good exact match.
   - **`shasum` fallback**: macOS has `shasum`; Linux has `sha256sum`. OK.
   - **Checksum comparison `!=`** — string compare, fine (both lowercase hex from tools).
   - **Quarantine strip after gate** — verified order. Good.
   - **`codesign -dv` parsing `Authority=`** with `head -1` — takes first Authority (chain root is last; first is leaf/actual signer). Reasonable.
   - **`case "$authority" in *"$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER"*)`** — substring match: allows `EVIL-Developer ID ... Expected Signer ...`? Substring match means authority containing expected anywhere. A CA could issue "Malicious Software CA / Expected Signer Ltd"? The Authority field contains the whole chain? `codesign -dv` prints multiple Authority= lines (leaf, intermediate, root); sed grabs only first. Substring match is loose — an attacker controlling a different identity whose name contains the expected substring passes. E.g., expected "Developer ID Application: Acme" would match "Developer ID A…

#!/usr/bin/env bash

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# check_action_pins.sh — SEC-08 (#796) AC1/AC4: mutable references to
# executable code are lint errors. Fails on any third-party GitHub Actions
# `uses:` ref that is not pinned to a full commit SHA.
#
#   bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh            # scan the repo (CI gate)
#   bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path DIR # scan DIR/*.yml (fixtures)
#
# Exempt:
#   - ./...          first-party repo-relative actions/workflows
#   - @<40-hex>      full commit SHA (the only accepted third-party form)
# Everything else (tags, branches, latest, main, master, short SHAs) fails.

set -eu

dir=".github/workflows"
if [ "${1:-}" = "--path" ]; then
  [ -n "${2:-}" ] || { echo "usage: $0 [--path DIR]" >&2; exit 2; }
  dir="$2"
fi

shopt -s nullglob
# Both modes share one shape: the root's workflows (either a
# .github/workflows layout or loose *.yml/*.yaml fixtures) plus EVERY
# composite action manifest at any depth — composite action steps can
# carry remote uses: refs, so they are part of AC1's threat surface.
files=("$dir"/.github/workflows/*.yml "$dir"/.github/workflows/*.yaml \
       "$dir"/*.yml "$dir"/*.yaml)
while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
  files+=("$f")
done < <(find "$dir" -name .git -prune -o -type f \( -name 'action.yml' -o -name 'action.yaml' \) -print0 2>/dev/null)

if [ ${#files[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "no workflow files found under $dir" >&2
  exit 2
fi

violations=0
for file in "${files[@]}"; do
  refs=$(grep -hoE '^[[:space:]]*(-[[:space:]]+)?uses:[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]]+' "$file" 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's/.*uses:[[:space:]]*//') || true
  [ -n "$refs" ] || continue
  while IFS= read -r ref; do
    [ -n "$ref" ] || continue
    case "$ref" in
      ./*) ;; # first-party repo-relative action/workflow
      docker://*)
        case "$ref" in
          *@sha256:*) ;; # digest-pinned container image
          *)
            echo "::error file=$file::unpinned container image ref: $ref"
            violations=$((violations + 1))
            ;;
        esac
        ;;
      *)
        sha="${ref##*@}"
        # A mutable ref whose NAME is exactly 40 chars would pass a pure
        # length glob — require hex digits (a commit SHA), nothing else.
        if [[ "$sha" =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$ ]]; then
          : # full 40-hex commit SHA — the only accepted third-party form
        else
          echo "::error file=$file::third-party action not SHA-pinned: $ref"
          violations=$((violations + 1))
        fi
        ;;
    esac
  done <<EOF
$refs
EOF
done

if [ "$violations" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "check_action_pins: $violations mutable third-party action ref(s)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "check_action_pins: OK (all third-party actions SHA-pinned)"

blocks.text:
## Cross-platform parity

Every shared setting and interactive prompt type must exist on BOTH the CLI
(`lib/src/cli/`) and the Flutter app (`flutter_app/lib/`) unless it is
**fundamentally impossible** on the target platform. When a setting or prompt
type is platform-only (e.g. MCP servers need process spawning — impossible on
web), it MUST be explicitly listed in `cliOnlySettings` or `appOnlySettings`
in `lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart` with a comment explaining WHY.

**Workflow when adding a new setting or interactive type:**
1. Add it to `SharedSetting` enum in `settings_registry.dart` FIRST
2. Implement on BOTH platforms (CLI + Flutter app)
3. If one platform genuinely cannot support it: add to the exemption set
   with a one-line reason comment
4. Run `dart test test/parity/` — the parity guard must pass

## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release commits from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` stay `github-actions[bot]`.
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` auto-releases a patch to pub.dev
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — intended. The version scheme is
  `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a
  monotonic `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again); the core and app pubspecs bump in lockstep.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate
  (issue #544: build 160, boot refactor created the platform env before
  `WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized`); boot stage order is pinned by
  `flutter_app/test/boot/app_boot_test.dart`.
- TestFlight external distribution (issue #239): the `submit_only` lanes
  (driven by build-mobile.yml / build-macos.yml) distribute every build
  straight to the EXTERNAL group — REQUIRED repo variables
  `TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP`, `BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL`,
  `BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_PHONE`, `BETA_APP_FEEDBACK_EMAIL` (lanes fail loudly
  at start without them). Pilot must WAIT for processing (skipping the wait
  silently skips distribution); `verify_external_distribution!` asserts
  group membership bounded — beta-review-pending is a neutral notice, a
  build never reaching the group fails the leg (self-filed issue).
- Manual App Store review: `release-appstore.yml` (workflow_dispatch:
  `version` + `platforms` ios/macos/both + `confirm` repeating the version)
  runs the `submit_for_review` lanes — pure pre-flight in
  `flutter_app/fastlane/appstore_preflight.rb` (plain-ruby tested) fails
  BEFORE any mutation; already-submitted versions are a green no-op;
  release-after-approval stays a manual ASC click
  (`APP_STORE_AUTOMATIC_RELEASE` repo variable flips it, E5). Grep-guards:
  `test/store_automation_guard_test.dart`.
- App Store content pipeline (no binary): store screenshots are COMMITTED
  goldens from `flutter_app/test/golden/store_screenshots_test.dart` (frame +
  inline en/ru copy in `store_marketing_frame.dart`) at

AGENTS.md notes: "CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies installers." — consistent with what I saw. Version scheme: `1.0.<counter>` now (0.1.x train dead: "the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>` train can never upload again"). 

This strengthens the pin finding: `pinned_cli_version: "0.1.452"` refers to the DEAD train (pre-App-Store-promotion), and even the historical release v0.1.452 predates the whole 1.0 era. Also its release assets certainly lack provenance. And the tag format is `v0.1.452` vs the pin `0.1.452` — URL mismatch. Three-layer problem with the baked pin:
1. Version format: repo tags are `v`-prefixed; the URL builder doesn't add `v` → 404 (E_ASSET_MISSING).
2. The pinned release (even addressed correctly) predates signed provenance → E_PROVENANCE_MISSING.
3. AGENTS.md says the 0.1.x train is dead — pinning it forever is odd; the follow-up (auto-bump) is acknowledged in the PR but there's no tracking issue mechanism mentioned.

The PR documents gap #2 only. Gaps #1 and #3 are not documented. #1 is a latent bug that will bite when someone sets a "correct-looking" pin (`1.0.458` instead of `v1.0.458`). I'll file it as IMPORTANT with a concrete fix (normalize: `case "$FA_VERSION" in v*) ;; *) FA_VERSION="v$FA_VERSION";; esac` — or document the contract + add a selftest assertion; better: accept the bare version in config and prepend `v` installer + generator validation `^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$`).

Hmm wait, let me double check the URL format used by installer for pinned: `https://github.com/$REPO/releases/download/$FA_VERSION` → `releases/download/0.1.452` → GitHub requires the exact tag name `v0.1.452` → 404. Confirmed. And for `latest`: `releases/latest/download` — works regardless of tag name. Good.

Also the E_ASSET_MISSING message would be the failure users see — which does NOT say "your pin is stale" — the "resolved version is always printed" claim mitigates (they see `→ Installing Fa version: 0.1.452`).

Now — additional things to check:

A. **`installer-smoke` ps1 leg on Windows**: unchanged install.ps1, no FA_VERSION use — fine.

B. **`installer-smoke` needs [binaries, release-provenance]** — on `release` event type published... the installer-smoke job `if:` condition? Let me look at the full job in current ci.yml to see event gating. Also whether `release-provenance` failure blocks `publish` (pub.dev). Publish is the pub.dev publish — independent. OK.

C. **`release` event double-fire**: binaries tolerates double-fire; release-provenance too (`--clobber`). OK.

D. **release-provenance `contents: write`** — needed for upload. Minimal-ish. OK.

E. **`printf '%s' "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" > signing.key`** — key material in workspace; then `rm`. If signing fails (bad key), the step fails BEFORE rm → key file remains in workspace (runner is ephemeral; but upload-artifact steps in other jobs don't run here). Low risk. SUGGESTION: use `mktemp` under `$RUNNER_TEMP` + `trap` cleanup, or pass via stdin (`openssl dgst -sign /dev/stdin`? openssl needs a seekable key file typically; `process substitution` works in bash). I'll suggest writing to `$RUNNER_TEMP` and cleaning up in a shell trap. Also: masked? GitHub auto-masks secret values in logs; a RSA PEM secret is multi-line — GitHub only masks single-line matches... Actually GitHub masks secrets in logs regardless of format? For multi-line secrets, masking doesn't work well. The key isn't echoed though. Fine.

F. **openssl key format assumption**: `FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY` must be a PEM RSA private key (`openssl dgst -sign` accepts PKCS#8/PKCS#1). The staged key: `.worktrees/issue-795-796/.fa-release-signing.key` — untracked, not in the diff. Can't verify. The doc says import then delete. OK.

G. **Self-test coverage gap**: no assertion that the EMBEDDED pem is parseable/matches the signing key. Concrete suggestion (prevents this exact class of silent breakage): in `release-provenance`, compare `openssl rsa -in signing.key -pubout | sha256sum` against a `SHA256(pubkey)` constant... but the embedded key lives install.sh in the repo — the job would need to extract it: `sed -n '/BEGIN PUBLIC KEY/,/END PUBLIC KEY/p' site/install.sh > embedded.pem && openssl pkey -pubin -in embedded.pem -noout` (parse check) and diff against `pub.pem`. Excellent, cheap, catches (a) scanner mangling, (b) key rotation drift. I'll make this an IMPORTANT recommendation inside the blocking PEM comment (or separate suggestion). I'll fold it into the blocking comment as the "why CI didn't catch it" + fix verification.

H. **installer-verify job on Windows?** Not needed (install.sh is unix). ubuntu+macos matrix — fine.

I. **selftest `expect_fail` uses `grep -q "$2"`** — fine. `dd` bit-flip at seek=10 on .sig — the sig is binary; flipping byte 10 → invalid sig. Good. Note: `printf 'X' | dd bs=1 seek=10` — fine.

J. **selftest PATH shim**: `PATH="$shim:$PATH"` — the installer resolves curl/openssl from PATH; shim only has xattr. Good. But — on Linux, `xattr` may not exist; real_xattr empty → shim uses /usr/bin/true. OK.

K. **selftest runs installer via `sh "$INSTALLER"`** — POSIX sh. OK.

L. **installer-verify caches/timeout**: timeout 10min fine.

M. **PR claims "verified block-identical after placeholder expansion"** — verified by my regeneration (byte-identical). Good; no finding.

N. **`supply-chain`/`dep-audit`/`installer-verify` all `needs: changes`** — run on every PR regardless of path (by design). But `needs: changes` + no `if:` means they run even for docs-only PRs (fine, cheap). But do they get skipped when changes says docs-only? No `if` on those jobs → they always run. Their intent says "no path gating". OK.

O. **quality-gate `needs` now includes supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-verify** — and the loop checks results. Note: quality-gate `if: always()` + fail on non-success/skipped. OK.

P. **E_ASSET_MISSING message references `dart build cli`** — pre-existing content, but note `cp build/out/bundle/bin/fah` — whatever, pre-existing.

Q. **Race between `gh release download` and `--clobber` upload of SHA256SUMS while installer-smoke installs** — smoke needs provenance success first. OK.

R. **`installer-smoke` sh leg**: sets FA_VERSION to ref_name (e.g. `v1.0.458`); URL `releases/download/v1.0.458` — valid tag. ✓. So smoke works; only the baked-pin default path is broken.

S. **Backups**: `rm -f "$target"` before cp — if download corrupt, nothing installed (verified). But note: on E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH etc., a PREVIOUSLY-installed fa remains (not removed) — "nothing installed" means no NEW install; existing binary stays. That's reasonable behavior.

T. **`mkdir -p "$install_dir/lib"` + lib copy `|| true`** — pre-existing pattern.

U. **Security check on `FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER` substring matching** — flag as SUGGESTION (anchor match: authority should START with expected, i.e. `"$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER"*`).

V. **`sed -n 's/^Authority=//p' | head -1`** — on newer codesign, `-dv` prints `Authority=Developer ID Application:...` first line = signing cert. OK.

W. **install.sh `set -eu` and `dl_ok`** — fine.

X. **`fetch` uses curl `-fsSL`** — no `--retry`. Transient network → hard abort. SUGGESTION: add `--retry 3`. Minor.

Y. **curl/wget presence**: if neither exists → wget fails. Pre-existing.

Z. **Dependabot group `"*"`** — pattern `*` in quotes; fine.

One more important angle: **the PR mixes #801 into its diff** — reviewers see 24 files; after #801 merges it'll shrink. Not a finding per se; the PR description declares it. OK.

2. And/or validate in `gen_installers.dart`: accept `vX.Y.Z` (or bare `X.Y.Z` + normalize) and hard-error otherwise, documenting the contract next to `pinned_cli_version`.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER` substring match is too loose**

```sh

blocks.text:
Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 814
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/814
- **Title**: fix(security): installer verifies pinned version + provenance before install
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-795` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 24
- **Additions**: +1043
- **Deletions**: -276
- **Created**: 2026-09-22T08:57:18Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-22T19:04:50Z

## PR Description

Closes #795 (SEC-07, MEDIUM).

**Stacked on #801 (SEC-08) — merge #801 first.** This branch contains #801's commit plus the one below; after #801 merges, this PR shows only the installer work.

## What

`site/install.sh` stops trusting `releases/latest` blindly:

1. **Pinned by default (contract 1).** `install-config.yaml` gains `install.pinned_cli_version: "0.1.452"`; the generator injects it as the `FA_VERSION` default. `FA_VERSION=latest` is the explicit override; the resolved version is always printed (`→ Installing Fa version: …`).
2. **Provenance gate BEFORE install and BEFORE quarantine-strip (contract 2).** Default trust path = **signed checksums**: the release's `SHA256SUMS` must carry a valid openssl RSA signature from the release-signing key. Trust anchor = the public key embedded in the installer (public material); private key = the `FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY` repo secret — a channel separate from the release assets, so a checksum file served from the same compromised source as the binary cannot vouch for itself. Fail-closed named errors: `E_PROVENANCE_MISSING`, `E_PROVENANCE_INVALID`, `E_CHECKSUM_MISSING`, `E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH`, `E_ARCHIVE_CORRUPT`, `E_CODESIGN_INVALID`, `E_SIGNER_MISSING`, `E_SIGNER_MISMATCH` — never best-effort.
3. **macOS (contract 3).** Quarantine-strip + ad-hoc re-sign run only AFTER the gate passes. `FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER` (optional) enforces a code-signature identity: invalid signature → `E_CODESIGN_INVALID`; identity mismatch → `E_SIGNER_MISMATCH`; no identity when one is expected → `E_SIGNER_MISSING`.
4. **Generator (contract 5).** `scripts/gen_installers.dart` renders `{{PINNED_VERSION}}` from `install-config.yaml` (hard-errors when unset); `site/install.sh.template` and the generated `site/install.sh` carry the identical verifying variant (verified block-identical after placeholder expansion).

## CI end-to-end

- New `release-provenance` job (tag/release builds, after `binaries`): aggregates every `fa-*` asset into `SHA256SUMS`, signs it with openssl (`FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY` secret; openssl is preinstalled on runners — **no new CI dependency**, no cosign), self-checks the signature, uploads `SHA256SUMS` + `SHA256SUMS.sig`. **Fail-closed:** secret unset → job red, no provenance published.
- `installer-smoke` now installs the just-signed release (`FA_VERSION=$\{{ github.ref_name }}`, `needs: [binaries, release-provenance]`).
- New `installer-verify` job (ubuntu + macos, EVERY PR — AC4): runs `scripts/installer_verify_selftest.sh` against local fixture releases.

## Verification (all run locally on macOS)

- AC1: bit-flipped fixture → `E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH`, exit 1, **nothing installed**.
- AC2: missing `.sig` → `E_PROVENANCE_MISSING`; corrupted sig → `E_PROVENANCE_INVALID`; both abort with nothing installed.
- AC3: valid fixture → installs and runs; version line printed; `xattr` PATH-shim proves the quarantine strip ran ONLY after verification (and never in any abort case).
- AC4: the selftest is the fixture matrix; CI runs it on every PR (both legs).
- Production trust path proven end-to-end: signature made with the real private key verifies against the EMBEDDED public key with no test overrides, and installs.

## Gaps (documented, not weakened)

- **`FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY` secret must be set** (repo admin action — this account has no admin). Until then every release build goes red at `release-provenance` and install.sh aborts `E_PROVENANCE_MISSING` on those releases. The private key for it is staged at `.worktrees/issue-795-796/.fa-release-signing.key` (untracked, matching the embedded public key) — import into the secret, then delete the file.
- The baked default pin (0.1.452) predates signed releases: default installs abort fail-closed until `install.pinned_cli_version` is bumped to the first signed release (follow-up: have `auto_release.sh`/the release flow bump it per release).
- Release CLI binaries are **ad-hoc** codesigned today; the provenance chain is the signed checksums. When Developer ID signing lands for the CLI binaries, bake `FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER` into the installer to enforce the publisher identity.
- `install.ps1` (Windows) and `install_local.sh` keep their current behavior — parity is a follow-up (issue non-goal: this card scopes install.sh + its generator).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# install.sh — non-interactive one-line installer for the Fa CLI
#              (flutter_agent_harness). Works when piped:
#                curl -fsSL "https://fa1.dev/install.sh" | sh
#
# What it does:
#   1. Detects OS and architecture.
#   2. Downloads the PINNED Fa release (FA_VERSION overrides; the resolved
#      version is printed) from GitHub Releases.
#   3. Verifies the artifact's provenance BEFORE installing: the release's
#      SHA256SUMS manifest must carry a valid signature from the embedded
#      release-signing key, and the archive must match the signed checksum
#      (SEC-07 #795 — fail-closed on any missing/invalid provenance).
#   4. Installs it to a directory on your PATH (macOS quarantine is stripped
#      only AFTER verification).
#   5. Prints a concise setup recipe and exits.
#
# For interactive configuration (provider, model, API key), run:
#   curl -fsSL "https://fa1.dev/setup.sh" | sh
#
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#  DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE BY HAND. It is generated from site/install-config.yaml
#  by `dart run scripts/gen_installers.dart`.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

set -eu  # no pipefail: dash (Ubuntu sh) lacks it

REPO="IstiN/flutter_agent_harness"
BINARY="fa"

# ── Output helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
say() {
  printf '%s\n' "$*"
}

info() {
  printf '\033[1;34m→\033[0m %s\n' "$*"
}

ok() {
  printf '\033[1;32m✔\033[0m %s\n' "$*"
}

warn() {
  printf '\033[1;33m!\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2
}

err() {
  printf '\033[1;31m✘\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2
}

# ── Banner ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
say ""
say "  ███████╗ █████╗       ████████╗███████╗██████╗ ███╗   ███╗██╗███╗   ██╗ █████╗ ██╗"
say "  ██╔════╝██╔══██╗      ╚══██╔══╝██╔════╝██╔══██╗████╗ ████║██║████╗  ██║██╔══██╗██║"
say "  █████╗  ███████║█████╗   ██║   █████╗  ██████╔╝██╔████╔██║██║██╔██╗ ██║███████║██║"
say "  ██╔══╝  ██╔══██║╚════╝   ██║   ╚════╝  ██╔══██╗██║╚██╔╝██║██║██║╚██╗██║██╔══██║██║"
say "  ██║     ██║  ██║         ██║   ███████╗██║  ██║██║ ╚═╝ ██║██║██║ ╚████║██║  ██║███████╗"
say "  ╚═╝     ╚═╝  ╚═╝         ╚═╝   ╚══════╝╚═╝  ╚═╝╚═╝     ╚═╝╚═╝╚═╝  ╚═══╝╚═╝  ╚═╝╚══════╝"
say ""
say "  Fa installer — flutter_agent_harness CLI"
say ""


# ── 0. Platform check ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# This script is for Unix-like shells. Native Windows users should use the
# PowerShell installer instead. Git Bash / MSYS / Cygwin can run this script,
# but the PowerShell installer is the recommended Windows path because it
# configures the user PATH and environment variables correctly.
case "${OSTYPE:-}" in
  msys*|cygwin*|mingw*)
    warn "you appear to be running in a Bash emulation layer on Windows."
    say ""
    say "  For the best Windows experience, use the PowerShell installer:"
    say ""
    say "    irm https://fa1.dev/install.ps1 | iex"
    say ""
    exit 0
    ;;
esac

# ── 1. Detect OS/arch ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
os=""
arch=""
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Linux*)     os=linux ;;
  Darwin*)    os=macos ;;
  *)
    err "unsupported OS: $(uname -s)"
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) arch=arm64 ;;
  armv7l)        arch=arm ;;
  *)
    err "unsupported architecture: $(uname -m)"
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

asset="fa-${os}-${arch}.tar.gz"

# ── 2. Resolve install directory ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# Prefer a directory already on PATH, falling back to ~/.local/bin.
# (POSIX-only syntax below: Ubuntu's /bin/sh is dash, no arrays/[[]]/pipefail.)
install_dir="${FA_INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"
# Only auto-switch to a PATH directory when the user did not explicitly pick
# an install directory. FA_INSTALL_DIR must win so CI/tests can install to a
# temp location without adding it to PATH first.
if [ -z "${FA_INSTALL_DIR:-}" ]; then
  case ":${PATH}:" in
    *":$install_dir:"*) ;;
    *":$HOME/.local/bin:"*) install_dir="$HOME/.local/bin" ;;
    *":$HOME/bin:"*) install_dir="$HOME/bin" ;;
  esac
fi

mkdir -p "$install_dir"
target="$install_dir/$BINARY"

# ── 3. Resolve version and download URLs ────────────────────────────────────
# SEC-07 (#795): the default install is PINNED to a known-good release.
# FA_VERSION overrides it explicitly (FA_VERSION=latest tracks the moving
# latest release); the resolved version is always printed.
FA_VERSION="${FA_VERSION:-0.1.452}"
if [ "$FA_VERSION" = "latest" ]; then
  release_base="https://github.com/$REPO/releases/latest/download"
else
  release_base="https://github.com/$REPO/releases/download/$FA_VERSION"
fi
# FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL exists for the verification self-test (local fixture
# "releases"); production installs never set it.
release_base="${FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL:-$release_base}"
info "Installing Fa version: $FA_VERSION"
asset_url="$release_base/$asset"
sums_url="$release_base/SHA256SUMS"
sig_url="$release_base/SHA256SUMS.sig"

fetch() { # fetch <url> <out-file>
  if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    curl -fsSL "$1" -o "$2"
  else
    wget -qO "$2" "$1"
  fi
}

# ── 4. Download release + provenance, verify BEFORE installing ──────────────
info "Downloading Fa for ${os}-${arch}..."
dl_ok=false
tmp_archive="$(mktemp 2>/dev/null || mktemp -t fa-archive)"
if fetch "$asset_url" "$tmp_archive"; then
  dl_ok=true
else
  warn "Download failed: $asset_url"
fi

if [ "$dl_ok" != true ]; then
  err "E_ASSET_MISSING: no prebuilt binary is available for ${os}-${arch} right now."
  say ""
  say "  The installer tried to fetch:"
  say "    $asset_url"
  say ""
  say "  Common causes:"
  say "    • A release is still building — wait a minute and retry."
  say "    • This platform is not yet supported."
  say ""
  say "  To build from source (requires the Dart SDK):"
  say "    git clone https://github.com/$REPO"
  say "    cd flutter_agent_harness"
  say "    dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out"
  say "    cp build/out/bundle/bin/fah ~/.local/bin/fa"
  say ""
  exit 1
fi

# Provenance gate (SEC-07 #795): the checksum manifest is only trusted when
# it carries a valid signature from the release-signing key. The private key
# lives in the repository (FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY secret) — a channel
# separate from the release assets — so a checksum file served from the SAME
# compromised source as the binary cannot vouch for itself. Fail-closed:
# missing or invalid provenance never degrades to "install anyway".

  exit 1
fi

  err "E_PROVENANCE_MISSING: release $FA_VERSION publishes no SHA256SUMS.sig signature — refusing to install without provenance."

  exit 1

# self-test only.

[REDACTED:High Entropy String]/0Tg094
[REDACTED:High Entropy String]
PhEfPuI1BbH6frKA2swu3JECAwEAAQ==
-----END PUBLIC KEY-----'
if [ -n "${FA_SIGNING_PEM:-}" ]; then
  trust_pem="$FA_SIGNING_PEM"
else
  trust_pem="$(mktemp 2>/dev/null || mktemp -t fa-pem)"
  printf '%s\n' "$TRUSTED_SIGNING_PEM" > "$trust_pem"
fi

info "Verifying release provenance (signed checksums)..."
if ! openssl dgst -sha256 -verify "$trust_pem" -signature "$tmp_sig" "$tmp_sums" >/dev/null 2>&1; then

blocks.text:
The git blobs themselves contain the REDACTED placeholders. So the committed public key PEM is destroyed — replaced by literal `[REDACTED:High Entropy String]` strings. This is a **BLOCKING** finding: the embedded trust anchor is corrupt, so `openssl dgst -verify` will always fail (the PEM isn't valid base64 / not parseable), meaning every install aborts with E_PROVENANCE_INVALID. The installer is completely broken as merged.

Note the last line of the PEM body survived: `PhEfPuI1BbH6frKA2swu3JECAwEAAQ==` — that's the tail of a base64 body (ends with `CAwEAAQ==` which is the standard RSA public key ending). So the redaction tool that mangled this kept lines that looked like they had low entropy... Actually it replaced high-entropy-looking lines with the placeholder but kept lines with trailing content like `/Ushhzf6`? No wait, line 3 is `[REDACTED:High Entropy String]/Ush` — hmm, that suggests the placeholder replaced part of the line and the tail `/Ushhzf6` remained? Earlier read showed line 3 as `[REDACTED:High Entropy String]/Ushhzf6`. So the redaction replaced a prefix/portion of base64 lines but left partial tails. And the last body line survived entirely (`PhEfPuI1BbH6frKA2swu3JECAwEAAQ==`).

Regardless: the embedded PEM is mangled. This could be:
1. A secret-scanning push protection that rewrote the file during commit (GitHub push protection normally blocks, doesn't rewrite).
2. The PR author's local tooling (e.g., a "redact secrets" pre-commit hook).
3. The task environment intentionally redacting "high entropy strings" when preparing the branch.

Whatever the cause, as a reviewer I must flag it: the trust anchor embedded in the installer is invalid, openssl will fail to load it (`E_PROVENANCE_INVALID` always), so the installer cannot install anything (even legitimately signed releases). BLOCKING.

Also this makes the selftest pass claim suspicious — the PR says "Production trust path proven end-to-end: signature made with the real private key verifies against the EMBEDDED public key". With a mangled PEM, that can't be true for THIS commit. Unless the selftest used FA_SIGNING_PEM override (test-only override path) — that's the "no test overrides" claim contradiction. The selftest script sets FA_SIGNING_PEM for fixtures, so CI selftest would still pass while production is broken — a silent failure mode. Let me verify by reading the selftest.

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# installer_verify_selftest.sh — SEC-07 (#795) AC1–AC4: fixture-release IT
# for site/install.sh. Builds a local fixture "release" (asset + signed
# SHA256SUMS), points the installer at it via FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL with a
# throwaway trust anchor (FA_SIGNING_PEM), and asserts:
#   AC1  tampered asset (bit-flip)      → abort E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, nothing installed
#   AC2  missing signature / bad sig    → abort E_PROVENANCE_*, nothing installed
#   AC3  valid fixture                  → installs; the macOS quarantine strip
#                                        runs only AFTER verification (order
#                                        asserted via an xattr PATH shim)
#   AC4  CI runs this script on every PR (installer-verify job in ci.yml)
set -eu

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALLER="$REPO_ROOT/site/install.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fixture="$work/release"
install_dir="$work/bin"
mkdir -p "$fixture" "$install_dir"

# Same platform mapping the installer uses, so the fixture asset matches.
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*) f_os=macos ;;
  Linux*)  f_os=linux ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test platform"; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  f_arch=x64 ;;
  arm64|aarch64) f_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "skip: unsupported test arch"; exit 0 ;;
esac
asset="fa-${f_os}-${f_arch}.tar.gz"

# xattr PATH shim: logs every invocation — proves whether the quarantine
# strip ran (and it must only ever run in the verified-good case). The REAL
# xattr binary is resolved now and baked in (the shim must not find itself).
real_xattr="$(command -v xattr 2>/dev/null || true)"
shim="$work/shim"
mkdir -p "$shim"
cat > "$shim/xattr" <<SHIM
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$work/xattr.log"
${real_xattr:-/usr/bin/true} "\$@" 2>/dev/null || true
SHIM
chmod +x "$shim/xattr"

# Throwaway trust anchor for the fixture release.
openssl genrsa -out "$work/test.key" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl rsa -in "$work/test.key" -pubout -out "$work/test.pub" 2>/dev/null

# Fixture release: bundle/bin/fa + version.txt, like `dart build cli`.
mkdir -p "$fixture/bundle/bin"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho fa-fixture-0.0.0\n' > "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
chmod +x "$fixture/bundle/bin/fa"
printf '0.0.0-test\n' > "$fixture/bundle/version.txt"
tar -czf "$fixture/$asset" -C "$fixture" bundle

sums_tool() {
  if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum "$@"; else shasum -a 256 "$@"; fi
}

sign_fixture() { # sign_fixture <fixture-dir>
  (cd "$1" && sums_tool "$asset" > SHA256SUMS)
  openssl dgst -sha256 -sign "$work/test.key" \
    -out "$1/SHA256SUMS.sig" "$1/SHA256SUMS" 2>/dev/null
}

run_install() { # run_install <fixture-dir>; output captured, exit code returned
  (cd "$work" &&
    FA_INSTALL_DIR="$install_dir" \
    FA_VERSION="0.0.0-test" \
    FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL="file://$1" \
    FA_SIGNING_PEM="$work/test.pub" \
    PATH="$shim:$PATH" \
    sh "$INSTALLER" > "$work/out.log" 2>&1
  )
}

expect_fail() { # expect_fail <fixture-dir> <expected-error> <label>
  set +e
  run_install "$1"
  status=$?
  set -e
  if [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "FAIL ($3): installer exited 0, expected abort with $2"; sed -n '1,40p' "$work/out.log"; exit 1
  fi
  if ! grep -q "$2" "$work/out.log"; then
    echo "FAIL ($3): expected $2 in output, got:"; sed -n '1,40p' "$work/out.log"; exit 1
  fi
  if [ -e "$install_dir/fa" ]; then
    echo "FAIL ($3): installer left a binary behind — 'nothing installed' violated"; exit 1
  fi
  echo "ok  ($3): aborted with $2 (exit $status), nothing installed"
}

# ── AC2: fail-closed on missing / invalid provenance ────────────────────────
sign_fixture "$fixture"
cp -R "$fixture" "$work/release-unsigned"
rm "$work/release-unsigned/SHA256SUMS.sig"
expect_fail "$work/release-unsigned" "E_PROVENANCE_MISSING" "AC2 unsigned"

cp -R "$fixture" "$work/release-badsig"
printf 'X' | dd of="$work/release-badsig/SHA256SUMS.sig" bs=1 seek=10 conv=notrunc 2>/dev/null
expect_fail "$work/release-badsig" "E_PROVENANCE_INVALID" "AC2 bad-sig"

# ── AC1: tampered artifact (bit-flip inside the archive) ────────────────────
cp -R "$fixture" "$work/release-tampered"
printf '\x00' | dd of="$work/release-tampered/$asset" bs=1 seek=100 count=1 conv=notrunc 2>/dev/null
rm -f "$work/xattr.log"
expect_fail "$work/release-tampered" "E_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH" "AC1 tampered"

# Order assertion (AC3): the strip shim must NOT have run in any abort case.
if [ -f "$work/xattr.log" ]; then
  echo "FAIL (order): quarantine strip ran despite failed verification"; exit 1
fi

# ── AC3: valid fixture installs; strip only after verification ──────────────
if ! run_install "$fixture"; then
  echo "FAIL (AC3): valid fixture failed to install:"; sed -n '1,60p' "$work/out.log"; exit 1
fi
grep -q "Installing Fa version: 0.0.0-test" "$work/out.log" || {
  echo "FAIL (AC3): resolved version not printed"; exit 1
}
grep -q "Checksum manifest signature verified" "$work/out.log" || {
  echo "FAIL (AC3): provenance verification did not run"; exit 1
}
[ -x "$install_dir/fa" ] || { echo "FAIL (AC3): $install_dir/fa missing"; exit 1; }
[ "$(sh "$install_dir/fa")" = "fa-fixture-0.0.0" ] || {
  echo "FAIL (AC3): installed binary does not run"; exit 1
}
[ -f "$install_dir/version.txt" ] || { echo "FAIL (AC3): version.txt not installed"; exit 1; }
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin*)
    grep -q "com.apple.quarantine" "$work/xattr.log" 2>/dev/null || {
      echo "FAIL (AC3): quarantine strip did not run after verification on macOS"; exit 1
    }
    ;;
esac
echo "ok  (AC3): valid fixture installed; verification preceded install + strip"

# ── pinned default + latest override resolve (contract 1) ───────────────────
# (no network here — just assert the script carries a baked non-empty pin)
grep -q 'FA_VERSION="${FA_VERSION:-[0-9]' "$INSTALLER" || {
  echo "FAIL (contract1): no pinned default version in installer"; exit 1
}
grep -q 'FA_VERSION=latest' "$INSTALLER" || {
  echo "FAIL (contract1): no explicit latest override in installer"; exit 1
}
echo "ok  (contract1): installer pins a default version; latest is opt-in"

echo ""
echo "installer_verify_selftest: ALL GREEN (AC1-AC4)"

1. **`release-provenance` job**:
   - Downloads `fa-*` assets, creates SHA256SUMS, signs with openssl.
   - `sha256sum fa-* > SHA256SUMS` — the SHA256SUMS file contains lines like `<hash>  fa-linux-x64.tar.gz`. But wait — inside the `provenance` directory, `sha256sum fa-*` produces relative filenames (`fa-linux-x64.tar.gz`). Good — the installer's awk lookup matches `$2 == asset` where asset is `fa-${os}-${arch}.tar.gz`. OK.
   - **Issue**: the `sha256sum fa-* > SHA256SUMS` step happens BEFORE the secret check. If the secret is unset, the job fails — fine, fail-closed. But note `if [ -z "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" ]` — with `set -e`? Default GitHub run steps use `bash -e`. OK.
   - **Security issue — private key handling**: `printf '%s' "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" > signing.key` writes the private key to disk in the workspace. Then `rm -f signing.key pub.pem`. The workspace is ephemeral, acceptable practice, though could use /dev/stdin or a pipe. Minor. More important: the key is written to the repo checkout dir; if any later step uploaded the workspace it would leak, but there is none. Acceptable; maybe suggest `printf ... > "$RUNNER_TEMP/signing.key"` to avoid workspace persistence and accidental artifact upload. SUGGESTION.
   - **Race condition / TOCTOU**: `installer-smoke` needs `[binaries, release-provenance]`, and downloads from the release. OK.

Fine.

   - **Issue — SHA256SUMS contains only fa-* assets**: `gh release download --pattern 'fa-*'` also matches... `SHA256SUMS.sig`? No — `fa-*` doesn't match SHA256SUMS. But on a RE-RUN of release-provenance (or `--clobber` re-upload), `gh release download` would also download a pre-existing `SHA256SUMS`/`SHA256SUMS.sig`? No — pattern `fa-*` doesn't match those names. But wait: `fa-*` WOULD match `fa-...` assets only. OK.

   - **Notable**: `release-provenance` is NOT added to any aggregate gate (quality-gate is PR-only; publish/installer-smoke gates tags). installer-smoke needs it — good. But what about `publish` (pub.dev)? Publish doesn't need provenance — fine, out of scope.
   - **Key rotation concern**: no key rotation path documented; public key embedded installer means old installers verify old releases only. Rotation would need dual-key acceptance. This is future work; SUGGESTION-level.
   - **Real issue — `installer-smoke` Windows leg**: the ps1 installer has no provenance verification (documented gap). The smoke for `kind: ps1` runs install.ps1 — unchanged behavior, fine.

Let me check actual tags in this repo: `git tag | tail`. The changelog says v1.0.457. The pin `0.1.452` without `v` prefix would break the default install even if the PEM were intact. Let me verify tag naming.

2. **`installer-verify` job**: runs the selftest on ubuntu + macos every PR. Good. Note `needs: changes` — and the quality gate includes installer-verify. OK.

3. **supply-chain + dep-audit jobs** — these are from the stacked #801/#796 work? Wait, the commit 4d7d7894 is "fix(security): review follow-ups — hex SHA validation, pin freshness, scan depth" which is #801's content. The ci.yml diff includes supply-chain and dep-audit — are those part of #801 or this PR? The PR says #801 is "SEC-08" (pin freshness = check_action_pins.sh + dependabot + SHA pinning + permissions). The supply-chain/dep-audit jobs mention SEC-08 (#796). Hmm, but they appear in this branch's diff against main. Since the stacked PR isn't merged yet (main doesn't have it), the whole thing shows.

Actually wait — let me check whether supply-chain/dep-audit were added by commit 4d7d7894 (#801) or c72aab99 (this PR). Let me check per-commit.

4. The installer changes (site/install.sh):

The installer is dead on arrival for all users, and worse, the selftest passes because it overrides via FA_SIGNING_PEM — CI green while production broken. This is a BLOCKING finding.

But hmm — the env override means if an attacker can influence the environment (e.g., a malicious .env loaded by shell?), they could inject their own trust anchor. Shell env injection for curl|sh is a stretch; it's for testability. It's a documented test hook in a public installer — an attacker who controls the env already controls PATH (can shim curl/openssl). Not a real finding; maybe SUGGESTION to note it's ignored unless... eh. Actually worth a low-severity note: the test override `FA_SIGNING_PEM` is available in the production script; combined with `FA_RELEASE_BASE_URL` override, the production installer's entire trust path can be silently redirected. Anyone running `curl | sh` with attacker-controlled env is already owned, so this is defense-in-depth documentation. SUGGESTION.

   - **`shasum` fallback**: macOS has `shasum`; Linux has `sha256sum`. OK.
   - **Checksum comparison `!=`** — string compare, fine (both lowercase hex from tools).
   - **Quarantine strip after gate** — verified order. Good.
   - **`codesign -dv` parsing `Authority=`** with `head -1` — takes first Authority (chain root is last; first is leaf/actual signer). Reasonable.
   - **`case "$authority" in *"$FA_EXPECTED_SIGNER"*)`** — substring match: allows `EVIL-Developer ID ... Expected Signer ...`? Substring match means authority containing expected anywhere. A CA could issue "Malicious Software CA / Expected Signer Ltd"? The Authority field contains the whole chain? `codesign -dv` prints multiple Authority= lines (leaf, intermediate, root); sed grabs only first. Substring match is loose — an attacker controlling a different identity whose name contains the expected substring passes. E.g., expected "Developer ID Application: Acme" would match "Developer ID A…

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# check_action_pins.sh — SEC-08 (#796) AC1/AC4: mutable references to
# executable code are lint errors. Fails on any third-party GitHub Actions
# `uses:` ref that is not pinned to…

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# check_action_pins.sh — SEC-08 (#796) AC1/AC4: mutable references to
# executable code are lint errors. Fails on any third-party GitHub Actions
# `uses:` ref that is not pinned to a full commit SHA.
#
#   bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh            # scan the repo (CI gate)
#   bash scripts/check_action_pins.sh --path DIR # scan DIR/*.yml (fixtures)
#
# Exempt:
#   - ./...          first-party repo-relative actions/workflows
#   - @<40-hex>      full commit SHA (the only accepted third-party form)
# Everything else (tags, branches, latest, main, master, short SHAs) fails.

set -eu

dir=".github/workflows"
if [ "${1:-}" = "--path" ]; then
  [ -n "${2:-}" ] || { echo "usage: $0 [--path DIR]" >&2; exit 2; }
  dir="$2"
fi

shopt -s nullglob
# Both modes share one shape: the root's workflows (either a
# .github/workflows layout or loose *.yml/*.yaml fixtures) plus EVERY
# composite action manifest at any depth — composite action steps can
# carry remote uses: refs, so they are part of AC1's threat surface.
files=("$dir"/.github/workflows/*.yml "$dir"/.github/workflows/*.yaml \
       "$dir"/*.yml "$dir"/*.yaml)
while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
  files+=("$f")
done < <(find "$dir" -name .git -prune -o -type f \( -name 'action.yml' -o -name 'action.yaml' \) -print0 2>/dev/null)

if [ ${#files[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "no workflow files found under $dir" >&2
  exit 2
fi

violations=0
for file in "${files[@]}"; do
  refs=$(grep -hoE '^[[:space:]]*(-[[:space:]]+)?uses:[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]]+' "$file" 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's/.*uses:[[:space:]]*//') || true
  [ -n "$refs" ] || continue
  while IFS= read -r ref; do
    [ -n "$ref" ] || continue
    case "$ref" in
      ./*) ;; # first-party repo-relative action/workflow
      docker://*)
        case "$ref" in
          *@sha256:*) ;; # digest-pinned container image
          *)
            echo "::error file=$file::unpinned container image ref: $ref"
            violations=$((violations + 1))
            ;;
        esac
        ;;
      *)
        sha="${ref##*@}"
        # A mutable ref whose NAME is exactly 40 chars would pass a pure
        # length glob — require hex digits (a commit SHA), nothing else.
        if [[ "$sha" =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$ ]]; then
          : # full 40-hex commit SHA — the only accepted third-party form
        else
          echo "::error file=$file::third-party action not SHA-pinned: $ref"
          violations=$((violations + 1))
        fi
        ;;
    esac
  done <<EOF
$refs
EOF
done

if [ "$violations" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "check_action_pins: $violations mutable third-party action ref(s)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "check_action_pins: OK (all third-party actions SHA-pinned)"

## Cross-platform parity

Every shared setting and interactive prompt type must exist on BOTH the CLI
(`lib/src/cli/`) and the Flutter app (`flutter_app/lib/`) unless it is
**fundamentally impossible** on the target platform. When a setting or prompt
type is platform-only (e.g. MCP servers need process spawning — impossible on
web), it MUST be explicitly listed in `cliOnlySettings` or `appOnlySettings`
in `lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart` with a comment explaining WHY.

**Workflow when adding a new setting or interactive type:**

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: The embedded trust-anchor PEM is corrupt — every production install fails `E_PROVENANCE_INVALID`**

As committed on this branch (verified in the git blob of `site/install.sh` **and** `site/install.sh.template`), the public-key body inside `TRUSTED_SIGNING_PEM` has been destroyed — the base64 lines were replaced by literal `[REDACTED:High Entropy String]` placeholder text (only fragments like `.../Ush`, `.../OKhzSE6...` and the last line `PhEfPuI1...CAwEAAQ==` survived):

```
$ sed -n '/BEGIN PUBLIC KEY/,/END PUBLIC KEY/p' site/install.sh | sed '1d;$d' > /tmp/k.pem
$ openssl pkey -pubin -in /tmp/k.pem -noout
Could not read key of Public Key from /tmp/k.pem      # exit 1
```

Consequences:

- `openssl dgst -sha256 -verify` cannot parse the PEM, so **every** install — including of a legitimately signed release — aborts fail-closed with `E_PROVENANCE_INVALID` ("the release channel may be compromised"). The installer is dead on arrival.
- **CI stays green anyway**: `installer_verify_selftest.sh` overrides the trust anchor via `FA_SIGNING_PEM="$work/test.pub"`, so the selftest never exercises the embedded key. The PR's claim "signature made with the real private key verifies against the EMBEDDED public key" cannot be true of this commit. (It looks like a secret-scanner false-positive mangled the high-entropy *public* key text; regardless of cause, this is what would merge.)

Fix:

1. Restore the real PEM in **both** `site/install.sh.template` and `site/install.sh` (they must stay block-identical after generation).
2. Better: keep a single copy — add `install.signing_public_key` to `install-config.yaml`, render it via a `{{SIGNING_PEM}}` placeholder in the generator, so the key text exists in exactly one file and future rotations can't drift.
3. Add the tripwires that would have caught this (see the selftest and `release-provenance` comments): assert the embedded PEM parses, and assert in CI that the embedded key equals the public key derived from `FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY`.

If the mangling is an artifact of local scanning tooling rather than the pushed commit, re-verify the PR head — the CI tripwire is what guarantees it stays correct either way.
"}

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Baked pin `0.1.452` can never resolve — repo tags are `v`-prefixed**

The installer builds:

```sh
release_base="https://github.com/$REPO/releases/download/$FA_VERSION"   # FA_VERSION=0.1.452
```

GitHub release-download URLs require the **exact tag name**. This repo's 412 tags are all `v`-prefixed (`v0.1.452` exists; `0.1.452` does not; current train is `v1.0.45x`). So the default path hits `releases/download/0.1.452/...` → 404 → `E_ASSET_MISSING`, not the documented `E_PROVENANCE_MISSING`.

This is worse than the documented "pin predates signed releases" gap: when a signed release lands and someone bumps `pinned_cli_version` to the natural-looking `1.0.458`, the default install still 404s. Nothing validates the format:

- `gen_installers.dart` only checks non-empty (no `^v?\d+\.\d+\.\d+$` validation).
- The selftest's contract-1 check only greps for a non-empty `[0-9]` default — it never resolves the URL.
- The CI smoke passes because it sets `FA_VERSION: ${{ github.ref_name }}` (`v`-prefixed), so the tag-format contract is never exercised.

Suggested fix (any one, ideally the first two):

1. Normalize in the installer: `case "$FA_VERSION" in v*) ;; *) FA_VERSION="v$FA_VERSION";; esac` before building `release_base`.
2. And/or validate in `gen_installers.dart`: accept `vX.Y.Z` (or bare `X.Y.Z` + normalize) and hard-error otherwise, documenting the contract next to `pinned_cli_version`.
3. Add a selftest assertion that the baked pin matches the tag convention.
"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: No tripwire that the embedded public key matches `FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY`**

This self-check only proves the signature verifies against the public key **derived from the secret itself** — it can never detect drift between the secret and the key actually **embedded in the installer**:

```yaml
openssl rsa -in signing.key -pubout -out pub.pem 2>/dev/null
openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pub.pem -signature SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
```

If the embedded PEM in `site/install.sh` drifts (mangled text, partial key rotation, template regeneration from a stale config), every release still publishes "valid" provenance while **no installer on earth can verify it** — all installs fail `E_PROVENANCE_INVALID` and CI is green. That is exactly the failure class this PR ships with today.

Cheap, permanent fix — extend this step:

```bash
# The installer's trust anchor must be THIS key's public half.
sed -n "/BEGIN PUBLIC KEY/,/END PUBLIC KEY/p" site/install.sh > embedded.pem
openssl pkey -pubin -in embedded.pem -noout          # parses at all?
cmp embedded.pem pub.pem || {
  echo "::error::embedded TRUSTED_SIGNING_PEM in site/install.sh does not match FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY — installs would fail E_PROVENANCE_INVALID"
  exit 1
}
```

(`site/install.sh` is checkout-able here: add a `actions/checkout` step or move the check into the `installer-verify` job.)

+tmp_sig="$(mktemp 2>/dev/null || mktemp -t fa-sig)"
+if ! fetch "$sums_url" "$tmp_sums"; then
+  err "E_PROVENANCE_MISSING: release $FA_VERSION publishes no SHA256SUMS — refusing to install unverified binaries."
+  rm -rf "$tmp_archive" "$tmp_sums" "$tmp_sig"
+  exit 1
+fi
+if ! fetch "$sig_url" "$tmp_sig"; then
+  err "E_PROVENANCE_MISSING: release $FA_VERSION publishes no SHA256SUMS.sig signature — refusing to install without provenance."
+  rm -rf "$tmp_archive" "$tmp_sums" "$tmp_sig"
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+# Trust anchor: the release-signing public key (public material, embedded
+# here at generation time). FA_SIGNING_PEM overrides it for the fixture
+# self-test only.
+TRUSTED_SIGNING_PEM='-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----
[REDACTED:High Entropy String]
[REDACTED:High Entropy String]
[REDACTED:High Entropy String]/Ushhzf6
[REDACTED:High Entropy String]
[REDACTED:High Entropy String]
[REDACTED:High Entropy String]
[REDACTED:High Entropy String]/OKhzSE6DK5pQne9PO77ybJw0O5dDxju
[REDACTED:High Entropy String]
[REDACTED:High Entropy String]
[REDACTED:High Entropy String]/0Tg094
[REDACTED:High Entropy String]
+PhEfPuI1BbH6frKA2swu3JECAwEAAQ==
+-----END PUBLIC KEY-----'
+if [ -n "${FA_SIGNING_PEM:-}" ]; then
+  trust_pem="$FA_SIGNING_PEM"
+else
+  trust_pem="$(mktemp 2>/dev/null || mktemp -t fa-pem)"
+  printf '%s\n' "$TRUSTED_SIGNING_PEM" > "$trust_pem"
+fi
+
+info "Verifying release provenance (signed checksums)..."
+if ! openssl dgst -sha256 -verify "$trust_pem" -signature "$tmp_sig" "$tmp_sums" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  err "E_PROVENANCE_INVALID: SHA256SUMS signature verification FAILED for release $FA_VERSION — the release channel may be compromised. Nothing was installed."
+  rm -rf "$tmp_archive" "$tmp_sums" "$tmp_sig"
+  [ "$trust_pem" = "${FA_SIGNING_PEM:-}" ] || rm -f "$trust_pem"

```sed

```
Line 1: `TRUSTED_SIGNING_PEM='-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----` → `1s/^.*BEGIN/-----BEGIN/` — greedy `^.*BEGIN` matches up to the LAST "BEGIN" → replaces everything through "BEGIN" with `-----BEGIN` → `-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----` ✓. Last line: `-----END PUBLIC KEY-----'` → `$s/END.*$/END PUBLIC KEY-----/` — `END.*$` greedy matches from first "END" → `-----END PUBLIC KEY-----` ✓. Clever. BUT edge: what if the PEM body contains a line with "BEGIN" or "END"?? Base64 alphabet has no such substring guarantee... base64 can contain "BEGIN" as a substring? Base64 chars are A-Za-z0-9+/ — "BEGIN" consists of valid base64 chars (B,E,G,I,N) — theoretically a body line could contain "BEGIN"... but the sed range `/BEGIN PUBLIC KEY/,/END PUBLIC KEY/p` — the pattern is "BEGIN PUBLIC KEY" WITH SPACE — spaces never appear in base64 body lines. So the range match is safe. And the `1s`/`$s` normalizations apply only to first/last extracted lines. ✓ Safe.
